title: Optimal partial plank coverings
summary: A plank of width $w$ in a Euclidean space is the set of points lying between two parallel hyperplanes at distance $w$ from each other. Bang's theorem says that if a family of planks covers a convex body $K$, then their total width is at least the width of $K$, that is, the width of the thinnest plank containing $K$. We study a quantitative variant of this problem in the case where the total width of the planks is fixed. How should the planks be placed so as to cover as much of the volume of the body as possible?
